newsitem.title: INDIA: India sees 97/98 inflation at 6.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: India sees 97/98 inflation at 6.8 pct.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday that the government estimates that wholesale price inflation will average 6.8 percent in 1997/98 (April-March) over the current fiscal year.
Chidambaram's estimate, provided in remarks to parliament on the 1997/98 budget, was the most precise inflation forecast which the government has given for the coming fiscal year.
Earlier this month the Finance Ministry said inflation in 1997/98 was expected to average between 6.5 and 7.0 percent.
"There is no reason to believe inflation will get out of line," Chidambaram said.
The year-on-year inflation rate as measured by the wholesale price index fell to 7.78 percent in the week ended on March 1 from 7.91 percent the previous week.
The rate stood at 5.13 percent in the week ended March 3, 1996.
In his reply to the debate on his proposed 1997/98 budget, Chidambaram said the government aimed to break long-term inflation expectations.
He said the government would not hesitate to import wheat, edible oil or sugar to plug any supply shortfall.
He appealed to farmers in Punjab state to turn over surplus wheat supplies to the public distribution system instead of withholding them.
Chidambaram reiterated that the government's highest priority was to bring down the fiscal deficit.
He said there were indications that tax revenues might exceed earlier expectations for the 1996/97 year ending on March 31. He did not elaborate.
Chidambaram admitted that there were gaps in the budget in the areas of infrastructure and power.
"There are some gaps," he said. "But we have time and in consultation with the power minister we can come up with a good programme for power generation and public investment in power.
"Public investment must lead the way. We will find a way so that substantial public investment in power will be made in the next year."
